doc.title: Howard Alden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Musical parents and early records
summary: His parents loved music without being musicians; their records of Goodman, Basie, Miller and Dorsey drew him in.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Did you get influence from your family? Your parents, were they musical?

I’d say they were musical but they weren’t musicians. You know they had a lot of good records around the house. They had everything from jazz to light classical stuff and some show tunes and stuff like that. And when I was very young I came across some old 45 rpm records and one of them I remember was a small group of Benny Goodman, one was a Count Basie with his rhythm section, there was like a Glenn Miller record and some 78s of Tommy Dorsey’s band and stuff like that. And I was drawn to those. I was really interested in them. And like I said when I started playing the stringed instruments, when I was ten, I was drawn to that kind of music, and then especially when I heard the records with the jazz guitarists.
